summary.text: A 51-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder, taking olanzapine 10 mg and lorazepam 1 mg at bedtime for three to four years, presented to the emergency department unconscious after an alleged ingestion of 10 tablets of olanzapine 10 mg about eight hours earlier. He had no history of diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, kidney disease or tuberculosis, and no smoking or alcohol use.

On admission his temperature was 36.83°C, pulse 120 beats/minute, blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 28 breaths/minute and SpO2 90%. He was unconscious with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of E1V1 M1, constricted pupils and an otherwise normal cardiovascular, respiratory and abdominal examination. Laboratory results across days one to four are tabulated, and a chest X-ray was normal.

He was intubated, a Ryle’s tube was inserted and aspirated, the fluid was sent for forensic evaluation, and gastric lavage with 300 mL of normal saline was done with activated charcoal. Supportive care continued with ventilator support, intravenous antibiotics, pantoprazole, ondansetron and fluids on days one to five. A psychiatric evaluation could not be done while he was ventilated.

Examinations in the day paragraphs also recorded him unconscious with GCS E2VTM4 and later conscious and oriented with GCS E4VTM6 and E4V5M6, with SpO2 of 96% and 95% on room air on days four and five. He was discharged on the sixth day in stable condition on cefixime, nitrofurantoin, risperidone with trihexyphenidyl and lorazepam, and was asked to review after seven days.
